Situation1: A family member has a significant event they want to share with everyone.
Situation2: They scan items during a slow afternoon with a few customers in line.
Story: I stood behind the register, the familiar beep of the scanner echoing in the quiet store. It was a slow afternoon, just a handful of customers waiting patiently with their baskets. My phone buzzed in my pocket, and I glanced at the screen—my daughter’s name flashed, followed by a message: “Grandpa, can you join us on video? Jamie wants to tell everyone her big news!” My heart leapt. Jamie, my granddaughter, had been working so hard for this moment. I imagined her eager face, the family gathered around, waiting for me to join. But here I was, in my cashier’s apron, responsible for every item, every dollar, every customer. I could feel the weight of their expectant eyes, the unspoken demand to keep the line moving. My family wanted me present, truly present, for a milestone. My job needed me focused, attentive, reliable. I gripped the scanner, torn between the beep of the register and the call of my family, caught in the space between two worlds that both needed me, right now.
